messages:
jess: quick heads-up — running longctx stress with INT8 + aggressive compaction enabled and seeing steady memory growth over ~20M tokens. p50 latency stable but resident set keeps climbing.
kevin: can you paste the perf profile / heap snapshot? is this only on a specific kernel selection path?
morgan: saw something similar yesterday on the hybrid-kernel path (int8 optimized matmul) — fragmentation spikes when small slot reuse is prioritized. attaching quick trace.
jess: attaching snippet from the nightly run:
```
allocs: +1.8GB over 12h
avg slot reuse rate: 72%
page evict count: 8421
compactions triggered: 15 (each ~120ms)
latency delta (p50): +12ms, p95: +48ms
recall (eval suite): -0.9% absolute vs bf16 baseline
```
anita: @jess @kevin thanks — did the run toggle the dormancy threshold or the eviction policy? i.e. LRU per-slot vs page-granular?
jess: dormancy=30s, eviction=slot-lru, compaction threshold=0.35. kernel strategy: prefer int8-kernel-v2, fallback to fp16-kernel on mismatches.
perf-bot: perf alert — heap_growth_rate high for service=runtime-gpu-03, rule=kv_mem_growth, severity=warning
kevin: hypothesis: int8 kernels have smaller working set per slot but produce more micro-fragmentation because quantized pages are smaller and compaction merges are more frequent. compaction + frequent batching changes could cause eviction thrash.
morgan: yep — when batching heuristic lowers max_batch_len to favor latency, we get more small writes to KV (many short sequences), which prevents contiguous page reuse. that plus compaction churn seems to be the accelerator.
anita: what about trying page-granular eviction for INT8 models and disabling compaction while slot fragmentation > 0.4? we should measure recall impact.
jess: ran a quick A/B locally: page-evict + compaction-off -> memory steady, growth delta ~0.1GB/12h, latency +4ms, recall loss reduced to -0.3%.
evidence:
```
config A (slot-lru + compaction): mem +1.8GB, recall -0.9%
config B (page-evict + compaction-off): mem +0.1GB, recall -0.3%
```
kevin: promising. can you capture kernel selection logs for both configs? we need to ensure fallback doesn't trigger extra copies (FP16 fallback can spike memory).
jess: logs show int8-kernel hits 91% in config A, 88% in config B, fallback copies to fp16 negligible (<1%).
morgan: another angle — batching heuristic: bump min_batch_fill to prefer slightly larger batches for int8 models so we get longer contiguous KV patterns. tradeoff: p50 +6ms but p95 unchanged.
anita: propose action items: 1) run 24h A/B on staging with page-granular eviction + compaction deferred, 2) telemetry add: per-model fragmentation ratio, compaction time, page-reuse rate, 3) experiment batching min_fill bump for int8 models, 4) add rollback knob to re-enable compaction for high-recall routes. owners: @jess (1,2), @morgan (3), @kevin (4).
jess: noted, starting staging job now. will post results and heap diff. :rocket:
kevin: quick perf note — also look at kernel selection latency for sequences >2k. int8 kernels sometimes have nonlinear perf cliff when seq_len crosses threshold because they switch block-size. might be related to compaction timing.
morgan: good call — i'll add a kernel selection telemetry flag to trace when kernel path changes mid-request.
jess: bump — staging finished preliminary 24h: mem growth flat, compaction-off reduced CPU compaction cycles by 93%, recall delta now -0.25%. full results uploading to the perf dashboard.
anita: awesome. next steps: if 72h looks good, promote config as default for int8 model family and add conservative compaction that only runs during low qps. :thumbsup:
